misconceptions.description: Treating validity as a fixed property of test items rather than of the inferences drawn from scores
misconceptions.trigger: learner says 'this is a valid test' without specifying what inference it supports
misconceptions.feedback: Validity is always about inferences. The same test items can support a valid inference in one context and an invalid one in another. State the inference first.

misconceptions.description: Writing wrong-answer options as arbitrary fillers rather than misconception probes
misconceptions.trigger: learner generates distractors that no real student would believe
misconceptions.feedback: Each distractor should map to a real misconception. If a distractor is not chosen by anyone, it carries no diagnostic information; rewrite or remove it.

misconceptions.description: Assuming any item type can validate any objective regardless of cognitive level
misconceptions.trigger: learner pairs an MC recognition item with a Create-level objective
misconceptions.feedback: The item must operate at the same Bloom level as the objective's verb. Recognition cannot validate Create. Rebuild one or the other.

misconceptions.description: Believing high reliability automatically guarantees validity
misconceptions.trigger: learner argues that since the test is consistent, it must be valid
misconceptions.feedback: Reliability is necessary, not sufficient. A test can consistently measure the wrong construct (reliable but invalid). Validity requires both consistency and the right inference.
